clue.text: Internal organs last to be damaged by bomb

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here as VI

indicators.note: being damaged leaves the word last broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb blast leaves the body's inner organs as the last things harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be damaged' signals the anagram; the V1 flying bomb is written with Roman-numeral letters, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitals is a plural noun for the body's essential inner parts such as heart and lungs.

clue.text: Service dress

parts.note: reads like a military uniform, but means what a priest wears to take a church service

explanation.surface: A soldier's uniform for parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a robe worn by clergy while conducting worship.

clue.text: Part of whip, but no good

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though, meaning but

explanation.surface: Someone says a piece of the whip is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The thong is the leather lash at the end of a whip.

clue.text: Boy's pulse raised

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: boy is the definition

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word reads it from the bottom up

parts.note: dal is the Indian word for lentils and other pulses

explanation.surface: A boy's heart rate goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is an everyday word for a boy or young man.

clue.text: Touched a female — made much of grabbing cape

indicators.note: grabbing means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: someone feted has been celebrated and made much of
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A woman is touched and fussed over by someone snatching her cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts C inside FETED to make FECTED, after A and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched and affected both mean emotionally moved by something.

clue.text: Footballer knowing his beer?

parts.note: fly is British slang for shrewd or knowing
a half is a half-pint of beer, the classic British pub order

explanation.surface: A footballer who knows his ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballer is a rugby one: a fly-half is the rugby union position that directs play.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-half is a player position in rugby football, so the player is a footballer.

clue.text: Very difficult positions for the hands

definitions.meaning: extremes of hardship or danger, desperate straits
hands and feet are the body's outer limbs

explanation.definitionFit: Extremities means both dire predicaments and the far parts of the body such as hands and feet.

clue.text: Can Beth assemble a vehicle?

parts.note: a can is a tin
Beth and Lizzie are both pet forms of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Beth can put a car together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb of a question but gives TIN; Beth leads to Lizzie through their shared full name Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin Lizzie was the nickname for the Ford Model T car, an early motor vehicle.

clue.text: Snug the Lion goes here, suggests playwright

parts.note: snug means cosy and dry, sheltered from the weather
a lion's lair is its den

explanation.surface: Snug, who plays the Lion in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is sent somewhere by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Snug is the joiner who plays the Lion in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so the theatrical surface hides a cosy lion's home.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet and dramatist who wrote many plays.

clue.text: Tablet for dental hygiene problem

definitions.meaning: a flat inscribed slab fixed to a wall
the film of bacteria that builds up on teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Plaque names both a commemorative wall tablet and the bacterial deposit on teeth.

clue.text: Fencing turning out to carry message

indicators.note: to carry means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: splay means to spread or turn outwards
word can mean a message, as in sending word

explanation.surface: A fencer's moves are spun into a way of passing a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' signals the container; splayed feet are turned outwards, which is the sense of 'turning out' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is the art of fencing with blades.

clue.text: Aussie beer is insubstantial

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a can of beer
thin and cheap, like flimsy metal

explanation.definitionFit: Tinny is Australian slang for a can of beer and also means flimsy or cheaply made.

clue.text: Fantastic -—- out of debt! The sum's the same, however you look at it

definitions.text: The sum's the same, however you look at it

parts.note: magic means wonderful or fantastic
to be square is to have settled up and owe nothing

explanation.surface: Wonderful news, debts cleared, and the totals agree from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic square is a grid of numbers whose rows, columns and diagonals all add up to the same total.

clue.text: Slight indisposition putting agent under-wind making things worse

indicators.note: in a down entry, the second piece goes under the first

parts.note: a chill is a minor illness such as a cold
a factor is an agent who acts for someone, as in buying and selling

explanation.surface: A slight illness, with a wind adding to the misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places FACTOR beneath CHILL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind chill factor is how wind makes the temperature feel colder than it is.

clue.text: Losing head in fervour and passion

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: fire is ardour or fervour

explanation.surface: Fervour and passion make someone lose their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' takes the F off FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, a strong passion.

clue.text: Exhausted, first back in compound

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front of the answer
back means the little word in is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
trite means overused, worn out, exhausted

explanation.surface: Worn out, someone goes back inside first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'first' fixes its position; 'Exhausted' reads as tired but means hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a chemical compound, a salt of nitrous acid.

clue.text: Inviting son to home to relax

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the clue's letters so they can settle into a new order

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking a son round to unwind at home sounds appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relax' rearranges S (son) with TO, HOME and the second TO; that final 'to' looks like part of 'to relax' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means appetising or attractive, so tempting and inviting.

clue.text: Part of temple wall is to make solid sound

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to freeze is to turn a liquid solid

explanation.surface: Part of a temple wall must be made firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' gives a word that sounds like FREEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorated band along the upper part of a classical temple wall.

clue.text: Tough taken to prison, we hear, for remorseless flogging

parts.note: hard means tough

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a cell is a prison room

explanation.surface: A hard man is jailed for a merciless beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns CELL into its sound-alike SELL; flogging is British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sell is aggressive, high-pressure salesmanship, a relentless way of selling.

clue.text: Appear to have cigarette

definitions.meaning: to turn up or arrive, as in people rolling up

explanation.definitionFit: Roll up means to arrive, and a roll-up is a hand-made cigarette.

clue.text: Carriage finds one path negotiable

indicators.note: a negotiable path can be wound through, so the letters of one path are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carriage finds a path it can travel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Agree painter has created fabulous creature

parts.note: to chime is to agree or fit in
RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: An artist has made a mythical beast to everyone's agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fire-breathing monster from Greek myth, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Pick out sweets with hard centres, say

indicators.note: say means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: chews are chewy sweets, here with hard middles

explanation.surface: Selecting chocolates with firm fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a word that sounds like CHEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick out and to choose both mean to select.

clue.text: Takes advantage of area transport

parts.note: buses are a form of transport, and to bus is to transport

explanation.surface: Someone exploits the local bus service.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse is to exploit or take unfair advantage of someone.

clue.text: Scrooge's reaction to Christmas starts to become awful habit

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Scrooge's grumpy response to the festive season grows into a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge, in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, dismisses Christmas with 'Bah! Humbug!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful exclamation is Scrooge's famous dismissal of the festive season.

clue.text: With nothing to do on a desolate trip

indicators.note: a trip, as in a stumble, upsets the letters of on a desolate

explanation.surface: Someone bored on a dreary journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but signals rearranging ON A DESOLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: At a loose end is an idiom for being idle with nothing to occupy you.

clue.text: Almost losing knight near beginning

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: nearly means almost
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is almost lost near the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means near the beginning of a period or process.

clue.text: Electrically, attempt to get round resistance?

definitions.text: Electrically, attempt to get round resistance?

indicators.note: getting round means one word goes around the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An electrician tries to work around resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get round' puts R inside SHOT; a short circuit lets current bypass the intended resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrics a short circuit is current taking a path that bypasses the proper resistance.

clue.text: Anglican responsibility for subcommittee

parts.note: a task is a duty or responsibility
taken as written
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A church responsibility given to a smaller committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a small group set up for a specific job, like a subcommittee.

clue.text: "Charge!" — first word Jack heard from giant?

definitions.meaning: a price asked for a service

definitions.text: first word Jack heard from giant
definitions.meaning: the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk roars a four-part chant, and this is its opening word

explanation.surface: In the fairy tale, the giant's battle cry greets Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'Charge!' look like a battle cry, but it means a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge made for a service.

clue.text: Expressing annoyance, finding Sunday tedious

parts.note: wearing means tiring or tedious

explanation.surface: Someone finds Sundays dull and grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is cursing, a way of venting irritation.

clue.text: Doctor with another side to him: a gardener

definitions.text: Doctor with another side to him
definitions.meaning: Stevenson's doctor whose dark other self is Mr Hyde
Gertrude, the famous English garden designer

explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll had the evil alter ego Hyde, and Gertrude Jekyll was a celebrated English garden designer.
